title: Backward sweep step for an arbitrary right stack
statement: Let $A$ be an alphabet, $S$ a state set, and $x$ a finite input word over $A$. Given an optional state $q$, a state $q'\in S$, an input-head position $p$, an integer frontier $z$, finite possibly blank-symbol stacks $l,r$, an output word, and a possibly blank symbol $b$, applying the action that writes $b$, moves the work head left, and enters state $q'$ yields the backward-sweep configuration with state $q'$, the same input-head position and output, frontier $z-1$, left stack $b::l$, and right stack equal to the tail of $r$.
hypotheses_covered: An optional state $q$ and a state $q'\in S$
An input-head position $p$ among the $|x|+2$ positions
replaced:
Consider the backward-sweep configuration of a one-work-tape machine with
(optional) state $q$, input-head position $p$, frontier $z$, left stack $l$,
an \emph{arbitrary} (possibly empty) right stack $r$, and output word
$\mathit{out}$. Applying the local sweep action that writes the
possibly-blank symbol $b$, moves the work head left, and enters state $q'$
produces the backward-sweep configuration with state $q'$, the same
input-head position and output, frontier $z - 1$, left stack
$b \mathbin{::} l$, and right stack the tail of $r$; when $r$ is empty, the
cell consumed is a blank beyond the stored zone.
